title: Automated Design Space Exploration in High-Level Physical Synthesis
evidence_span: The paper presents a robust physical-feedback-guided HLPS design-space exploration framework that automates iterative parameter tuning; author abstract reports mean Fmax 311.06 MHz versus 128.48 MHz Vitis/Vivado and 186.21 MHz academic solutions, with conditions and budget limits preserved in the assessment.
problem: Multi-die FPGA timing closure depends on interacting physical-synthesis parameters.
method_or_artifact: Implementation-feedback-guided search over device abstraction, ILP floorplanning, routing capacity and pipeline choices.
workload_or_benchmark: Six designs, seven design/device cases: Sextans, Callipepla, MM 10x13 on two devices, Serpens, NTT and GPT-2 Medium.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Alveo U55C/U280/U250 and Versal VHK158; EPYC 7742 host with 256GB DDR4-3200; up to four concurrent Vitis jobs.
baselines: AMD Vitis -O3 Explore with target-frequency backoff
metrics: Reported mean Fmax: 311.06 MHz DSE versus 128.48 MHz Vitis/Vivado and 186.21 MHz AutoBridge; headline ratio remains withheld pending matched-budget and baseline-failure review
limits: Fmax is not throughput or faster synthesis. AutoBridge fails one case; 1.67x matches unequal-population means, versus 1.65x on shared cases. Actions and time are cumulative, not independent ablations. No equal-budget superiority or independent acceptance.

evidence_locators.location: Table V, PDF page 8; supplementary denominator and runtime analysis
